_note: FIDELITY-AXIS designs. This is a DIFFERENT metric axis from benchmark/designs.json (token-cost). Fidelity designs measure GROUNDING RETENTION (fraction of task-needed facts still present in the loaded context) vs TOKEN SAVING. They answer 'does deferring/compressing lose the facts the task needs?', NOT 'how many always-on tokens'. Do not compare fidelity numbers against token-cost numbers: different axes, different units.

compare_to_axes.token_cost: benchmark/designs.json + run_designs.py (measures always-on tokens + rule-firing integrity; unit = tokens)
compare_to_axes.fidelity: this file + run_fidelity.py (measures grounding retention vs token saving; unit = fraction of needed facts retained)

F1_lossless_grounding.definition: Lossless deferral: full body loaded on demand when a task needs it (no compression). Grounding is a NULL CONTROL: retention must equal the monolithic baseline.
F1_lossless_grounding.claim: Grounding retention = 1.0 (identical to monolithic); lossless deferral loses no needed fact. Token saving comes from deferral, not from shrinking content.

F2_summarized_L033.definition: Lossy summarization at compression level 0.33 (structural operator: keep code/identifier lines, drop prose).
F2_summarized_L033.claim: Retention still 1.0 at level 0.33 (safe frontier lower bound); modest token saving.

F3_summarized_L050.definition: Lossy summarization at level 0.50 (measured safe frontier from the N=6 study).
F3_summarized_L050.claim: Retention 1.0 at level 0.50 (safe frontier); this is the maximum safe compression.

F4_summarized_L066.definition: Lossy summarization at level 0.66 (past the safe frontier).
F4_summarized_L066.claim: Retention DROPS below 1.0 (facts lost); large token saving but UNSAFE for fact-recall. Demonstrates the cliff.
